1_CURRENT_BALL_IMPROVEMENT: The only source whose export applied NO resize, so its stored pixels are original pixels. 1,263 ball boxes, median 9.1 px at native 1280x720 -- SMALLER than EyeCU's own ball median. 474 balls <=8 px as stored.
3,830 ball boxes across 55 matches and 6 leagues, real broadcast. Balls are LARGER than EyeCU's own (35 px vs 18 px at 1920-equivalent), so this is ball DIVERSITY, not tiny-ball supply.
1,251 keep-candidate images with the best ball boxes of the six, but one La Liga match only.
Ball-only with unlabelled humans; large balls; reference at best.
141 padded ball boxes across a few Premier League matches.
498 ball boxes, one match, boxes distorted by a 640x640 stretch.
2_FUTURE_CALIBRATION: Complete and verified: homography, fisheye intrinsics and extrinsics, undistortion maps, 65 pitch correspondences, for all 10 matches. Two independent routes agree to 9.8 px; 0.83 m median positional accuracy. Nothing else audited comes close.
Calibration and pitch-coordinate methodology, as reading material only -- GPL-3.0.
3_FUTURE_EVENTS: 23,663 BAS events, 12 classes, ms timestamps, player_id on 99.5%, alignable to video.
Action-centred sampling with replay groups; the export is organised around events even though it ships no event labels of its own.
4_FUTURE_IDENTITY_JERSEY: 15,041 readable jersey numbers on detections, plus team-left/team-right role split and 57 teams.
Full squad metadata, jersey numbers, persistent track_id -> player_id, but only 10 amateur matches and unusable boxes.
5_FUTURE_TRACKING_RESEARCH: Persistent identities, though with no occlusion gaps, so it does not exercise what a tracker must solve.
Designed as an external MOT benchmark; access currently BLOCKED_ACCESS (401).
Tracking pipeline ideas, GPL-3.0, reference only.

experiment_d_gate.question: SHOULD WE CREATE EXPERIMENT D?
what_changed: keremberke supplies 1,263 ball boxes at NATIVE resolution with no resize in the export chain -- the first source in any EyeCU audit where a small stored ball is a genuinely small ball. Its balls are smaller than EyeCU's own: 13.7 px vs 18 px at 1920-equivalent.

SoccerNet-V3 supplies 40,139 player, 2,948 goalkeeper and 3,402 referee boxes with goalkeeper and referee as DISTINCT classes, across 55 matches in 6 leagues -- the class distinction EyeCU needs and the diversity the six Roboflow sources could not provide.
Neither source overlaps EyeCU VAL or TEST.
what_has_NOT_changed: Still no large supply of genuinely tiny broadcast balls. Across everything audited, balls <=8 px in original terms remain rare.
A large correlated block from one match is still not diversity: RB_S6 remains 1,251 frames of one La Liga match.
blocking_conditions_before_D_can_be_desi: keremberke collapses goalkeeper AND referee into "player" (verified visually on yellow-kit officials). Mixing its human boxes as-is would damage the two classes EyeCU is weakest on. Either use it ball-only with its humans handled as ignore-regions, or relabel -- and neither is authorised yet.
SoccerNet-V3 label quality has not been visually verified on the downloaded payload yet, and its Staff members / Wall of players / Referee flag / card classes must be dropped rather than mapped.
SoccerNet-V3 ships an action frame plus up to 8 replay frames of the SAME action; replays are correlated by construction and must not be counted as independent images.
